ledger.note: 16 March 1355: Han Lin'er is proclaimed emperor of a restored Song at Bozhou. 'Han Lin'er was proclaimed emperor of a restored Song dynasty in Bozhou (in western Anhui) on 16 March 1355.' Era name Longfeng; Liu Futong is the strongman.

region.text: Jiangnan Province, led by Zhu Yuanzhang from 1356

ledger.note: May 1356: Han Lin'er names Zhu Yuanzhang head of Jiangnan Province. In May, Han Lin'er named him head of Jiangnan Province; Zhu 'still acknowledged his subordinate status' to Han and used the Longfeng era while Han lived, but ran his own administration. Drawn as a vassal tint until January 1367.

region.text: Shandong, where Mao Gui ran a functional administration

ledger.note: 1357 (bridging): Mao Gui's Shandong province. Between 1356 and 1359 the Song government set up five provinces. Mao Gui ran a functional administration in Shandong; the page gives the span, not the year, and the Liu Futong page says only that his forces later 'capture parts of Anhui and Shandong'.
June 1358: Liu Futong's army captures Kaifeng. 'His army captured Kaifeng, the first capital of the Song dynasty, in June 1358.' The Red Turban page dates the departure to 11 June 1358.

ledger.note: June 1358: the Song and the Yuan fight over Kaifeng and the Henan plain. Liu Futong's northern expedition (Mao Gui against Dadu from Shandong, a force in the Fen valley of Shanxi) lasts until Chaghan Temur's counteroffensive of 1359.
June 1358: the court moves to Kaifeng, the former Song capital.

ledger.note: 1359: Chaghan Temur drives the Song back from the Bozhou-Yingzhou base to Anfeng. Chaghan pushed Liu first to Yingzhou, then to Bozhou, then to Anfeng; the Red Turban page has the court remaining at Anfeng from 1359 to 1363. The page does not date each step.
10 September 1359: Chaghan Temur retakes Kaifeng. Chaghan Temur's counteroffensive forced the Song to withdraw from Kaifeng.

ledger.note: September 1359: the fighting over Kaifeng ends with the Song withdrawal; the court then survived in Bozhou and later Anfeng.
1359: the court moves to Anfeng. The Song court moved to and remained at Anfeng until 1363 (Red Turban page); the Han Lin'er page says it first survived at Bozhou.

June 1363: the court is moved to Chuzhou, inside Zhu Yuanzhang's territory. Chuzhou: from June 1363.

notes: Written for ea-06-x. Wikipedia has no article for the regime itself (Han Lin'er is the closest; the Chen Han page says no state link exists), so the dossier is read from the Han Lin'er, Liu Futong, Red Turban Rebellions and Hongwu Emperor pages. All keyframes are new circles and provinces. Disagreements between pages: end of the Song 1366 (infobox era) or January 1367 (regnal table and text); the 1363 move to Chuzhou is June (Han Lin'er) or soon after the February attack (Red Turban); Anfeng was taken by Zhang Shicheng's general Lü Zhen (Liu Futong page) in February 1363 although the Red Turban page says Zhang 'attacked' it; the Red Turban page puts the proclamation at Bozhou and the capital at Yingzhou. What the pages do not give: the year of the Shandong province, what became of Shandong and the other Song provinces, the three-army route of the 1357 expedition (the summariser's reading of the Han Lin'er page names Mao Gui, Guan Duo and Li Wu and Cui De only). Three Song events (1357, 1362, 1367 vassal end) are confidence 1 or 2 for that reason. The vassal relation of Zhu Yuanzhang to the Song is recorded here, as the suzerain, with counterpart zhu-yuanzhang-s-wu. Counterparts needing dossiers: yuan-dynasty (ea-06-a), zhu-yuanzhang-s-wu and zhang-shicheng-s-wu (this batch).
